source.citation: Hawkins, May, Pickett and Abell (1991), Benefits of NOAA-11 Channel #3 in Detection of Mesoscale Eddies in the Gulf of Mexico During Summer, pp. 356–360, in Proceedings: Eleventh Annual Gulf of Mexico Information Transfer Meeting, November 1990. OCS Study MMS 91-0040, published October 1991.
source.access: Original proceedings PDF acquired; actual PDF pages 345–347 / printed pages 356–358 reviewed. Authors explicitly identify Quiet in the same discussion. The dimensions are printed source approximations from August 12 and 19 imagery, not OSW graph or map readings.

coverage_interpretation: 396 numeric references across 136 source identities, including 162 size references owned by 87 identities; 49 size-reference gaps remain. Own numeric coverage remains 121 identities, with 15 lacking it. Quiet gains two approximate source-described SST axes, not a verified physical footprint or complete seasonal dimensions. The source identities are not a global physical census.
scope_limits: Hawkins, May, Pickett and Abell presentation at the November 1990 meeting, published October 1991 in MMS 91-0040; original PDF verified.
Source discussion links dimensions to August 12 and 19, 1990 imagery without independent values for each image. Neither a continuous interval nor a seasonal envelope is inferred.
Nearly 400 km is retained as approximate wording rather than a strict upper bound; 250–300 km is a source approximate minor-axis interval, with no representative midpoint.

SST appearance with drifting-buoy context, not a mathematically fitted ellipse or fixed outer-contour operator. Approximately 0.5°C edge contrast is neither an isotherm definition nor measurement uncertainty.
No diameter, ellipse area, physical geometry, lifetime, state containment, ranking, seasonal playback, runtime installation, or release.
Bosphorus model figure and historical Hot Core/Nelson/Quiet charts reviewed but no ambiguous flow or chart lines admitted as sizes. TIGER/AMIGO 91G-02 is retained as a future named hydrographic lead.
